title: Pinned-model fallback policy: region & variant failovers, deprecation grace
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: Customers can pin specific model versions for deterministic behavior. When a pinned model version becomes temporarily or permanently unavailable (regional outage, failed deployment, deprecation), we need a deterministic, observable, and policy-driven fallback flow that preserves SLAs and developer expectations.

Goals: Ensure stable behavior for pinned requests while minimizing surprise regressions in quality or latency. Provide clear controls (tenant-level and route-level) for allowing fallbacks, and surface telemetry and audit events when fallback occurs. Graceful handling of model deprecations and automated migration suggestions are required.

Scope: Implement server-side fallback orchestration and policy enforcement for pinned models in Hosted and Dedicated modes. Exclude on-prem air-gapped automated cross-region fallback (will surface as recommendation only). Integrate with performance profile publishing so fallbacks select a compatible performance profile and emit profiling events for billing and SLO attribution.

Design summary (high-level):
- Fallback precedence (configurable but default order):
  1) Local region, exact pinned model version (if available).
  2) Local region, compatible model variant (e.g., quantized / smaller architecture tagged compatible by model-onboarding).
  3) Cross-region, exact pinned model version (if tenant allows cross-region routing).
  4) Cross-region, compatible model variant.
  5) Unpinned best-effort model (last resort) with explicit audit log and developer warning header.
- Policy flags: tenant.allow_region_fallback (bool), tenant.allow_variant_fallback (bool), route.fallback_behavior = [deny|allow|defer_to_tenant]. Route-level settings override tenant-level.
- Deprecation handling: model onboarding includes a deprecation_date and migration_map. If pinned version reaches deprecation_date, we:
  * Mark pin as "deprecation-warning" and emit an admin notification/email to the tenant and the pin owner.
  * For pins older than grace_period (default 90 days) we auto-apply migration_map to suggest a new pin. Auto-unpin is NOT performed without tenant opt-in; instead we offer an automated migration PR (console + API) that can be accepted.
- Performance profiles: each fallback candidate must have a published performance_profile_id; the runtime will select the profile and attach profile metadata to the response and billing trace. If fallback increases latency/cost beyond thresholds, trace-level alert events are created.

API/Client contract:
- New response headers: X-Redwood-Fallback-Used: <none|variant|region|migrated|unpinned>, X-Redwood-Original-Pin: <model:version>, X-Redwood-Fallback-Candidate: <model:version>.
- If route.policy == deny and pinned model unavailable -> return 409 Conflict with structured JSON explaining reason and suggested action.
- If fallback used and route.policy == allow -> 200 with extra headers and an event logged to the pin audit stream.

Acceptance criteria:
- Runtime implements fallback precedence with tenant and route policy enforcement.
- Telemetry events emitted for each fallback decision: fallback_type, source_region, target_region, performance_profile_id, latency_delta, token_cost_delta.
- Console shows recent fallback incidents per-pin and per-tenant.
- Default tenant config allows region fallback but requires explicit allow for variant fallbacks.
- Deprecation flow: notifications sent at 30d, 14d, 3d before deprecation_date and a migration suggestion appears in Console.
- End-to-end integration tests cover exact-pin available, region outage, variant available, both unavailable -> unpinned fallback, and deprecation lifecycle.

Notes and trade-offs:
- We choose NOT to auto-unpin because it can silently alter model behavior; instead we provide guided migration and opt-in automation.
- Cross-region fallbacks may increase P99 latency — those are visible via trace-level tags and count against SLAs; recommend tenants configure route-level policy if latency-sensitive.
- Variant fallback requires robust compatibility metadata in model-onboarding. We will require model owners to publish a compatibility matrix for each model version to be eligible for variant fallback.

comments: 2026-02-11 — Triage: flagged as P1 due to recurring customer reports where pinned models fell back silently during cross-region maintenance. Assigned to Diego for implementation planning.

2026-02-18 — Design review completed with PM and DX: agreed that default tenant setting will allow region fallback but not variant fallback. Need to update onboarding catalog to include 'compatible_variants' field.

2026-02-25 — Engineering decision: implement policy as fast-path checks in router before queueing; add audit events early to avoid gaps in observability. Diego will own runtime changes; Aisha will own onboarding metadata schema changes.

2026-03-02 — Implementation: router check + header plumbing complete in branch feat/pin-fallback. Basic telemetry emitted (fallback_type, target_model). Integration tests added for local-region fallback. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/3245

2026-03-08 — QA: Found an edge-case where a variant marked compatible lacked published performance_profile_id, causing fallback to fail. Added validation during onboarding and an onboarding-gate that rejects incomplete variants.

2026-03-12 — Next steps: finish cross-region routing failover logic, wire Console display for per-pin incidents, and create migration suggestion UI. Schedule canary rollout behind feature-flag 'pin-fallback-enabled'.

Open items: finalize thresholds for automated alerting (suggested: >1% fallback rate in 10m window triggers paging), create runbook for high-fallback incidents, update SDK docs to describe new headers and error codes.
